title: Agnello in fricassea
subtitle: Italian egg-and-lemon thickened lamb stew
excerpt: Agnello in fricassea is an Italian lamb braise finished with beaten egg yolks and lemon juice, which thicken the sauce into a velvety, pale coating. The method is the Italian equivalent of the Greek avgolemono: egg and lemon transformed a plain stew into something rich and delicate. The lamb goes in as neck or shoulder, and it cooks for about an hour.
sourceNotes: Italian traditional recipe. Egg-and-lemon thickened lamb stews appear across central and southern Italy and follow the same ancient logic as Greek avgolemono. Method drawn from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Braise the lamb up to the point of adding the egg yolks. Add the yolks just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: An Italian braise thickened at the end with beaten egg yolks and lemon juice; the egg must be added off the heat to prevent it from scrambling and turning grainy.

content.text: is a lamb braise finished with egg yolks and lemon, which thicken and enrich the cooking juices into a pale, velvety sauce. The technique is the same as for Greek avgolemono. The lamb should be from the neck or shoulder, where there is collagen to keep it tender through an hour of cooking. The egg finish is added off the heat at the very end.

items.prepNote: or shoulder, cut into 4 cm chunks

content.text: Season {{lamb-neck}} of lamb. Heat the butter and oil in a casserole. Brown the lamb in batches, 5 minutes per batch. Remove. Cook {{onion}} of onion for 5 minutes, then add {{garlic}} of garlic for 1 minute.

Return the lamb. Add {{dry-white-wine}} of wine, let it reduce by half. Add {{stock-chicken}} of stock, the rosemary, and bay leaves. Cover and braise over low heat for 50 to 60 minutes until the lamb is tender. Remove the herbs.

Beat {{egg-yolks}} of egg yolks with the lemon juice. Remove the pot from the heat. Let it stop bubbling. Pour the egg mixture in slowly while stirring constantly. Return to the lowest possible heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens slightly. Do not allow it to boil. Stir in the parsley and serve immediately.

items.cause: Sauce was still boiling when the yolks were added.
items.fix: Let the pot cool for 2 minutes off the heat before adding the egg. The sauce should be warm, not bubbling.
Start with the juice of one lemon and taste before adding more. The lemon should be present but balanced.

content.text: Fricassea preparations are found across central and southern Italy, especially in Lazio and Campania where lamb is the preferred meat. The egg-and-lemon combination in Italian cooking predates French fricassee and has clear Mediterranean roots. It is a spring dish by tradition, made when young lamb is available and the lemons are bright.
